file.@1:
Chapter 2: The Janitor-Who-Looks-Like-That

The staircase seemed endless! Was there a mysterious floor between the third and the fourth ones? Could this be one of the secrets hidden inside the Tower-In-The-Middle-Of-The-Street? Igor had seen such things in movies, terror stories... His imagination ran wild, and he didn’t realize that the room was getting darker after every step he took. When he noticed that, it was too late: a complete darkness surrounded him!

file.@1: He thought about yelling out, but when the boy was about to do so, he saw a beam of light just ahead. Forgetting any security measures, he quickened his pace. When he finally arrived there, he saw a strange scene. It looked like a room with two escalators, one going up, the other, down. So far, everything was normal, but the steps were four or five times smaller than usual. Because of that, the "floor" had a very low ceiling. Even more absurd: the steps were moving very, very fast, and there were no handrails. They were sliding so fast that Igor was afraid he could not step on the right place.

file.@1:
From the top, he could see some people downstairs trying to climb the escalators. All of them, however, were falling down just the moment they put their feet on the fast steps and were eventually giving up. Igor tried to call them, but they did not seem to hear him. 
“Well”, he thought, “it is my turn to try”.

file.@1: Everything happened as Igor had predicted: immediately after he stepped on the escalator,  he fell. However, unlike what was happening to the people downstairs, the movement of the escalator ended up pulling him forward, and he soon found himself on the lower area. People who were there, trying to go up, became frightened. When Igor pulled himself together and took a look around, he saw that some of them were ratty, looking very tired. He stood up and his head almost reached the ceiling. Facing those people, the boy asked where he was, but got no answer for a while.

– Boy, didn't you pay attention to what the Janitor-Who-Looks-Like-That said?
– Janitor-Who-Looks-Like-That? What janitor? What did he say?
– Didn't he warn you about not going down the stairs? Didn't he say you were bringing the key to enter the city?

file.@1:
Igor remembered the strange man he found on the fourth floor, but that man hadn't said anything about entering a city. A city? What did that mean?
Realizing the confusion of the boy, the woman continued:
– Haven't you met the caretaker of the fourth floor? What did he say to you?
– He said I could go down because I was not carrying a key, I guess...

file.@1:
What were they talking about? What was that? The only thing he wanted at that moment was a way out. Igor ran and tried to climb the escalator, but, like everyone else, he fell back. The laughter was loud. Everyone was making fun of him. And, in a moment of desperation, he cried, without quite knowing why:
– I want to get out of here! I want to go down!

file.@1:
For no apparent reason, the crowd stopped laughing immediately. The expressions went from mockery to perplexity, and then to panic. The woman spoke again:
– Do not say that! You have to go up, not down. If you want to get out of here, you have to go up, not down!
– Too late – said another woman – he is already here.

file.@1:
"Who?", thought Igor, while looking around. At that moment, the boy saw the strange man people were calling the Janitor-Who-Looks-Like-That. He was standing close to the escalator and asked, with a strong voice, much firmer than that one Igor heard before from him:
– Who wants to go down?
The crowd was completely silent and immediately started pointing to the boy. The caretaker looked at him for some time, perplexed.

file.@1:
Soon they reached another escalator. Whoa! An escalator?! Yes, an escalator that was not there before. It had been a common staircase. Igor could still see those people and they seemed to have completely forgotten about him: they were, as before, looking at the fast steps and trying, unsuccessfully, to go up.
– Will we go down on this escalator?
– No. You will. I'm staying here.
